notes:
Prospect: VS Code extension that provides pair-programming style copilot for mid-size engineering teams.
Key ask: low-latency streaming for inline completions and real-time suggestions (editor experience must feel instantaneous).
Architecture notes from product: extension runs a local bridge that opens a persistent websocket to service; wants chunked streaming with delta patches to minimize cursor jitter.
Model/version strategy: want to pin models per extension release channel (stable/beta) and be able to rollback to a smaller quantized variant if latency/throughput becomes constrained.
Rate limits: require predictable soft limits and a backoff policy so the extension can display "throttled" gracefully rather than hard-fail. Also asking for per-api-key granular quotas and developer sandbox keys for internal teams.
Security: SSO/SAML + scoped service keys; must support EU data residency for EU customers and audit logging for feature flag changes.
Cost sensitivity: medium — willing to trade some cost for guaranteed sub-100ms first-token latency for hot users. Interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization profiles.
Quote from CTO: "If the in-editor latency is >120ms people perceive it as lag — we've got to be under that threshold for our power users."
Next: SE (Priya) to deliver POC test harness and sample VS Code patch that wires streaming events to editor decorations. Legal to confirm residency/retention answers by 2026-03-10.
summary: Pegasus Pair Labs is evaluating Redwood for their VS Code copilot extension. Primary focus on streaming completion latency, model pinning per release channel, predictable rate limits and EU residency. Moving into a short POC.
